full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the order dated 10.12.84 passed by the Additional District Judge 2nd Court, Dhaka in Misc. Appeal No. 154 of 1984 allowing the appeal ex parte and setting aside the order of dismissal dated 4.1.84 passed in Misc. Case No. 9 of 1983 and also setting aside the decree dated 20.1.83 passed in Title Suit No. 290 of 1980, 4th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and restoring the title Suit to its file and number would not be set aside. 

 2. The defendant opposite party No. 1 filed an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside decree dated 20.1.83 passed in Title Suit No. 290 of 1980 of the 4th Court of Subordinate Judge Dhaka. In the suit the defendant opposite party No. 1 entered appearance on getting summons and filed written statement but ultimately refrained from contesting the suit as a result the suit was decreed ex parte on 20.1.83. The application filed by the defendant No. 1 having been entertained the opposite party No. 1 was required to issue notice upon the opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 by post and for the same to be put in postal requisites on 11.12.83. The opposite party No. 1 having not complied with the said order 4.1.84 was fixed for putting in the postal requisites as a last chance. On 4.1.84 the defendant opposite party No. 1 having failed to put in the postal requisite in compliance of the Court's order, the Misc. Case No. 9 of 1983 was dismissed for default. Against the said order dated 4.1.84 passed in the said Misc. Case, the opposite party No. 1 preferred appeal before the learned District Judge. Dhaka which was submitted as Miscellaneous Appeal No. 154 of 1984. The said appeal was allowed by the learned District Judge ex parte in the absence of the petitioner and the order of dismissal dated 4.1.84 passed in Misc. Case No. 9 of 1983 was set aside and simultaneously the ex pane decree passed in Title Suit No. 290 of 1980 was also set aside and the suit was restored to its file and number. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order the petitioner obtained the instant rule. 

 4. Mr. Kh. Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the appeal was not maintainable in the form and manner it was filed, that no appeal lies as the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was dismissed for default at a very earlier stage for non-filing of the requisite and not at the stage when it was ready for hearing and in that view of the matter the learned appellate Court committed an error of law in his decision in allowing the same which has occasioned a failure of justice and for that matter the judgment and order is required to be set aside. By way of elucidating the point the learned Advocate submits that the appeal having been dismissed for default for non-filing of the postal costs at the stage when the case was not ready for hearing the order of dismissal should be deemed to be an order under Order 9 rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such not appealable and therefore learned court should have dismissed the appeal on the ground of maintainability." 

 5. Mr. SB Berua, appearing for the opposite party No. 1, submits that the order having been passed by the court-in the Misc. Case on an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure the provision of Order 9 rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure has no manner of application in the case. The language of Order 9 rule 2 runs as follows: 

 7. The next point Mr. Kh. Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits is that Order 43 rule 1(d) provides for an appeal against the judgment and order passed in such a proceeding which is contested, or at least in a matter which is ripe for hearing, and not in respect of an order which is passed at the initial stage as was done in the present case. Mr. Kh. Mahbubuddin Ahmed further submits that there is a difference between an order of dismissal passed for non-filing of the requisite at an early stage and the order passed at a later stage and therefore, dismissal of a case at an early stage of the proceeding for non-filing of the requisite remedy by way of appeal is not available. 

 8. It is contended by Mr. SB Barua, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1 that an order of dismissal for default under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is appealable under Order 43 rule 1(d) of the Code no matter whether the order is passed at the earlier or later stage. In the case of Abdul Majid Talukder Vs. Abdur Rob Talukder reported in 32 DLR page 57 the following principle is laid down: 

 "The distinction sought to be made between the word 'rejected' and the order 'dismissed' appears to be a distinction without a difference. The words 'rejected', 'struck of', 'closed', 'recorded' and 'dismissed' have similar import, but differently used with reference to the facts and circumstances of each case and there is no distinction between them in substance". 

 9. In the case of Md. Hashim Khan Vs. Major Fazal Elahi Khan reported in PLD 1959 Quetta I. a distinction to the general rule was sought to be made by a single judge who held: 

 10. This distinction which was sought to be made in the above noted case has been resolved in a number of cases of this court. The principle laid down by Ibrahim, J in the case of Abdur Rahman Maji and another Vs. Abdul Wadud Mia and another reported in 2 PLD (Dacca) 287 has been consistently followed in many cases and also in the case of Abdul Majid Talukder Vs. Abdur Rob Talukder reported in 32 DLR page 57 wherein it has been held: 

 "We are in respectful agreement with the opinion of Ibrahim, J. in the case of Abdur Rahman Maji (Supra) In our view, a defaulter whose application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure has been dismissed for default has a lawful remedy in an appeal under Order 43 rule 1(d). The expression 'rejected' is wide enough to include a dismissal for default under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Accordingly, we hold that such an order is appealable". 

 11. Since the statute provides remedy to the aggrieved person against whom application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure has been dismissed for default, whatever might be the stage of passing the order in the Miscellaneous Case I am quite in agreement with the decisions quoted above and find that the appeal arising out of the order of dismissal of the proceeding under Order 9 rule 13 Code of Civil Procedure is maintainable. 

 12. Mr. Kh. Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, next submits that the Misc. Case having been dismissed for default on 4.1.84 for not filing the requisites, the case was not ready and as such in the appeal the Miscellaneous Case could not have been disposed of on merit and in that view of the matter, the learned court committed an error of law in his decision in setting aside the ex parse decree dated 20.1.83 passed in Title Suit No. 290 of 1980 while disposing up the appeal and thus has exceeded his jurisdiction vested in him. 

 13. From the facts stated in the judgment of the court below it is found that the notice issued upon opposite party No. 2 and 2(a) was awaiting report and before the submission of the same the order of dismissal of the misc. case was passed by the Subordinate Judge for non-filing of the requisite. 

 14. The learned Subordinate Judge having passed the order dismissing the Misc. Case at the stage while the case was not ready for hearing as regard service it is held that the learned Court of appeal below committed an error of law in setting aside the order of the Subordinate Judge passed on 4.1.84 in the Misc. Case. Now it is to be seen whether the Court of appeal below was justified in setting aside the ex parte decree passed on 21.1.83 in Title Suit No. 290 of 1980 while setting aside the order of dismissal passed in Miscellaneous Case. As the Misc. Case No. 9 of 1983 was dismissed for non-filing of requisites without entering into the merits as to whether the defendant failed to appear and contest the suit after receipt of the summons in the suit or the defendant was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing and contesting the suit the appellate Court below committed error of law and exceeded his jurisdiction in setting aside the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 290 of 1980 and in that view of the matter the order of setting aside the ex parte decree and restoration of the Title Suit No. 290 of 1980 to its original file can not be sustained. 

 15. In the result, the rule is made absolute. The judgment and order of the appellate Court passed on 10.12.84 in Misc. Appeal No. 154 of 1984 is hereby set aside. The order dated 4.1.84 dismissing the misc. case for default is also hereby set aside and the case No. 9 of 83 is sent back to the Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka for hearing on merit after giving opportunity to the parties.
